validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and independently regulated. This row is the 'CTPL Expansion Project' -- a compressor-only expansion of the existing Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline (CTPL), filed under FERC Docket CP25-506-000 as part of a joint June 6, 2025 application with Sabine Pass Liquefaction (CP24-75-001) and Sabine Crossing (CP25-505-000) for the broader 'Sabine Pass Stage 5 Expansion Project' (Federal Register Notice of Application, 90 FR 26808, govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-06-24/pdf/2025-11578.pdf, verified via pdftotext -- the WebFetch HTML rendering of this same PDF hallucinated four different, wrong docket numbers, so the govinfo PDF was downloaded and extracted locally per the escalation rule). Cheniere's own Binding Open Season Notice (April 21, 2025, lngconnectionapi.cheniere.com/tempImages/CTPL-Open-Season.pdf) independently corroborates the same scope, capacity, and docket-adjacent facts. FERC's Notice of Intent (Aug 13, 2025) and Notice of Availability of the Draft EIS (April 8, 2026, 91 FR 17803) confirm the docket is still active and under NEPA review as of this sweep. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook tracks this exact project independently (project_key 'ctpl expansion project', operator 'Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline, L.P', docket CP25-506-000, 930 MMcf/d, in-service 2031) across every release from 2025-07 through 2026-08 -- not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' / 'Gas' are correct -- an NGA section 7(c) interstate/intrastate natural gas transportation-capacity expansion, not gathering or a distribution lateral. DUPLICATE: checked against the full roster and the wider Creole Trail family. P7797 is DISTINCT from P0283 (the Creole Trail main line, 94.8 mi/42in, already swept) and from P2522 (Creole Trail Pipeline Reversal Project / EIA's 'Creole Trail Expansion Project 2', a much older 2012-era, 104.3 mi/1500 MMcf/d, FERC Docket CP13-553 project that has cycled Approved/Cancelled/Approved repeatedly since 2018 and is unrelated to this 2025-filed, compressor-only, 930 MMcf/d, Docket CP25-506 project). It is also distinct from P5509 'Sabine Pass LNG Stage 5 Expansion Pipeline' -- see cross_row_leads; that PID more plausibly corresponds to the separate 'Sabine Crossing Pipeline' (Docket CP25-505-000, a new 55.6 mi/48in TX pipeline), not CTPL. No relabel/merge candidate found. ATTRIBUTION: Operator = 'Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline, L.P' confirmed as the FERC applicant of record and EIA's recorded operator name. Owner1 = 'Cheniere Energy' (100%) is confirmed by Cheniere's own Open Season Notice, which states CTPL 'is an indirect subsidiary of Cheniere Energy, Inc.' -- consistent with the same Owner1 convention already carried on the sibling rows P0283 and P2522 for this same pipeline family (Cheniere's actual corporate chain runs through the intermediate holding entity Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P., but GEM's own established convention across all three Creole Trail rows already records the ultimate public parent, so this is not a new attribution defect specific to this row). SPEC: see the per-unit fills[] records; every HAS_REF cluster's only current citation (https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines) is a navigation page that never states any of this row's values (confirmed by the builder's own existing_ref_checks) and has been replaced with the dated EIA release plus FERC/Cheniere documents that actually state each value. One minor EIA-internal wrinkle, not a GEM defect: EIA's own workbook briefly (2025-10 and 2026-01 releases only) mis-carried Miles=104.3 (the parent system's full length) on this compressor-only project before correcting to Miles=0 in the 2026-05 and 2026-08 releases -- the current, corrected release matches the sheet's LengthKnown=0.

cross_row_leads.facts: P5509 'Sabine Pass LNG Stage 5 Expansion Pipeline' has every spec blank. This FERC Notice of Application (Docket CP25-505-000, filed jointly 2025-06-06) describes a facility that may be the real referent: Sabine Crossing, LLC proposes ~55.6 miles of new 48-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline from the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal across Jefferson County, TX and into Liberty County, TX; a new Hampshire Compressor Station (four 52,500 HP units, 210,000 HP total); up to 2.7 Bcf/d delivered to the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal; estimated cost $1,626,222,797. Same joint filing as P7797's CP25-506-000; Draft EIS issued 2026-04-08 (91 FR 17803, federalregister.gov/documents/2026/04/08/2026-06766). Worth checking whether P5509 should be re-keyed to this Sabine Crossing Pipeline project rather than left as a near-empty placeholder.
